History:
• 3-day history of frequent loose/watery stools (~6–7 BM/day) beginning the day after eating Chinese takeaway  
• Intermittent cramp-like pain, left lower abdomen; non-radiating; comes and goes  
• Initial vomiting on day 1 (no blood); now resolved  
• Subjective fever at onset; currently afebrile but feels weak/shaky  
• No blood or mucus in stool, no melena, no persistent vomiting, no night sweats  
• Able to tolerate fluids; poor appetite—taking mainly soups/smoothies  
• One child vomited once; no other household members with diarrhoea  
• No prior similar episodes reported

Past Medical History:
• Asthma—well controlled with inhaler (type and dose not documented)  
• No other chronic illnesses reported  
• Allergies: not recorded  
• Medications: rescue/maintenance inhaler (name/dose/route/frequency not documented); no other medications

Physical Examination:
• Remote consult—no physical examination performed  
• General appearance (reported): feeling weak but alert  
• Abdominal exam, vitals, hydration status: Not recorded

Impression:
Most likely acute infectious gastroenteritis (viral or self-limiting bacterial) following recent takeaway meal.  
DDx (consistent with transcript):  
1. Acute viral gastroenteritis – classic short-course watery diarrhoea, initial vomiting, mild household spread.  
2. Acute bacterial food-borne infection – timing after takeaway and focal abdominal cramps raise possibility.

Management Plan:
• Conservative care: maintain oral hydration; advised oral rehydration salts (e.g., Dioralyte)  
• Symptomatic relief: paracetamol 1 g (two 500 mg tablets) up to QID as needed for fever/aches (dose per physician verbal guidance)  
• Rest: advised 2–3 days off work  
• Red flags/follow-up: return or seek care if symptoms worsen, if unable to keep fluids down, develop high fever, blood in stool, or if diarrhoea persists >3–4 days → consider stool culture and further evaluation  
• No antibiotics prescribed at this stage

Patient Summary:
Adult male with well-controlled asthma presents via telehealth with 3 days of watery diarrhoea, left-sided abdominal cramps, initial vomiting, and subjective fever after eating takeaway. Clinical picture most consistent with self-limited gastroenteritis. Supportive management and close follow-up arranged.

Key Takeaways:
• Drink plenty of clear fluids and use oral rehydration salts.  
• Take paracetamol for fever/discomfort.  
• Stay home from work for the next 2–3 days to rest and prevent spread.

Next Steps:
• Monitor symptoms; if not improved in 3–4 days or if red-flag signs appear, schedule in-person review and stool studies.  
• Routine asthma medication to continue as usual.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing elements: objective vitals, physical exam, allergy status, exact inhaler name/dose/frequency, medication reconciliation.  
• No transcript vs. DDx conflicts noted.  
• Transcript quality: clear audio; minor conversational filler but clinically adequate.
